# Tapproval

> Approve Claude Code's permission prompts from an Apple Watch. When the
> agent on your computer asks permission, the question appears on the
> watch, marked with one of five risk tiers, and one tap answers it.
> No account and no server of ours. Independent; not affiliated with Anthropic.

## What it does
- Approve or deny Claude Code permission prompts with one tap on the watch.
- Sorts every request into one of five risk tiers on the computer; the card
  shows the tier. Nothing is approved automatically unless the user turns
  that on, and a CRITICAL request never is.
- Shows which sessions need you, which are running and which are idle;
  read a conversation and reply, or start a new session from the watch.
- Multiple-choice questions arrive with the same choices as on the desktop.

## What it needs
- An Apple Watch running watchOS 10 or later.
- Claude Code on a Mac or a Linux machine.
- The free, open-source helper (MIT licence), which Claude Code installs
  when told: "Install the Tapproval plugin from marcobelini/tapproval-helper".
- Works on the same Wi-Fi, or away from home through a private travel address.

## Price
- The first 100 answers are free; then $5 once unlocks unlimited answers
  for good. No subscription. An optional $1 tip is offered too.
- Reading sessions and the day's overview stays free.

## Where to get it
- App Store, outside the EU for now: https://apps.apple.com/app/tapproval/id6805869018
- TestFlight beta, everywhere: https://testflight.apple.com/join/dW1tYBQG
- Helper source: https://github.com/marcobelini/tapproval-helper

## Privacy
Tapproval collects nothing: no accounts, no analytics, no servers of ours.
Prompts and conversations travel between the watch and the user's own
computer, directly or through an encrypted tunnel.
